title: Blender Conference 2026: the AI-enabled Tools & Workflows SIG
author: oscar_unrealizex
selftext:
Preface/disclosure: Hi everyone! I'm Oscar and I've got almost 2 decades doing all the Blender things. Wrote the book on Blender, brought Blender workflows to Pokemon, and I made the Seattle Blender User Group. For the last 2 years I've been working on a mesh reconstruction suite with [www.unrealizex.com](http://www.unrealizex.com) where we make 3D assets in as little as 1 credit, 1 image, 1 minute. Our process doesn't use generative AI, but this work means learning new AI workflows and engaging with the nuances and concerns of AI. I show some of this work, but it's not the focus of the talk.   


Here's my talk from the 2026 Blender Conference, the Blender + AI-Enabled Workflows SIG. The SIG covers some broader AI literacy, Blender's history with AI, the current guidelines and projects, and also reframing this discussion through the lens of "The Blender ethic." Namely: Software freedom, project sovereignty, open culture, and our history as technological tinkerers. 

  
I hope this has some useful information for you, and true to the SIG format, I'd love to hear your answers to the questions!

1. What was your dream to make/build/create...back when you were a kid?  
2. In 1 or 2 words, what is the BLENDER + AI-ENABLED TOOLS & WORKFLOWS thingy that you want to discuss?   
3. What do you HATE doing, and AI handles that chore? What do you LOVE doing, and AI augments that joy?  
4. Blender! AI! Open culture! Sharing! How are you living that Open Culture/Software Freedom life?
